description_full: Trustmark Corporation operates as the bank holding company for Trustmark National Bank that provides banking and other financial solutions to individuals and corporate institutions in the United States. It operates through General Banking and Wealth Management segments. The company offers checking, savings and money market accounts, and certificates of deposit, as well as certificates of deposit and individual retirement accounts; and treasury management services. It also provides loans comprising financing for commercial and industrial projects, income producing commercial real estate, owner-occupied real estate, and construction and land development; and installment and real estate loans and lines of credit. In addition, the company offers mortgage banking services, including construction financing, production of conventional and government-insured mortgages, and secondary marketing and mortgage servicing; wealth management and trust services, such as administration of personal trusts and estates; management of investment accounts for individuals, employee benefit plans, and charitable foundations; and institutional custody for large governmental entities and foundations, financial and estate planning, and retirement plan services. Further, it provides an intermediary vehicle for the provision of loans or investments in low-income communities. Trustmark Corporation was founded in 1889 and is headquartered in Jackson, Mississippi.

financial_summary: Trustmark Corporation is a mid-cap financial services business with a $2.8B market cap on $800M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $232M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.09× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 0.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 5.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 6.9% of the shares.
